title.en: Question word order and indirect questions
title.es: Orden en las preguntas y preguntas indirectas

summary.en: In a **direct question** the auxiliary goes before the subject: _Where does she work?_ In an **indirect question** (after _Could you tell me…_, _I wonder…_, _Do you know…_) the order goes back to a statement and there is no _do/does/did_: _Could you tell me where she works?_ When the question word **is the subject**, there is no auxiliary either: _Who called you?_
summary.es: En español decimos «¿Sabes dónde vive?» y «¿Dónde vive?» con el mismo orden de verbo. En inglés no: en la pregunta directa va el auxiliar (does she live) y en la indirecta, orden de frase afirmativa (where she lives).

form: Direct: **question word + auxiliary + subject + verb** (_What did you buy?_)
Subject questions: **question word + verb** (_Who lives here?_ _What happened?_)
Indirect: **introduction + question word + subject + verb** (_Do you know what time it starts?_)
No do/does/did and no inversion in the indirect part; the verb shows the tense (_what time it started_)
Yes/no questions become **if/whether** (_I wonder if he's free._)
A question mark is used only when the introduction is a question (_Can you tell me…?_ but _I don't know where she is._)

uses.text: **Polite requests for information**: _Could you tell me where the station is?_
**After I wonder, I don't know, I'd like to know**: _I wonder how much it costs._
**Yes/no information questions**: _Do you know if the shop is open?_

note.en: If and whether are both possible. Whether is a little more formal.
note.es: If y whether valen los dos; whether es algo más formal.

uses.text: **Subject questions have no auxiliary**: _Who wrote this?_ not _Who did write this?_
**Prepositions** often go at the end: _Who are you waiting for?_ In formal writing: _For whom…?_

mistakes.wrong: Do you know where does he live?
mistakes.right: Do you know where he lives?

why.en: In the indirect part use statement order, with no do/does.
why.es: Tras Do you know… no hay auxiliar ni inversión: where he lives.

mistakes.wrong: I don't know what time is it.
mistakes.right: I don't know what time it is.

why.en: Keep subject + verb order after the question word.
why.es: El orden es sujeto + verbo: what time it is.

mistakes.wrong: Who did call you this morning?

why.en: When who is the subject, don't add did.
why.es: Si who es el sujeto, no hace falta did.

mistakes.wrong: Can you tell me where is the post office?
mistakes.right: Can you tell me where the post office is?

why.en: The verb be also goes after the subject in an indirect question.
why.es: El verbo be también va detrás del sujeto: where the post office is.

mistakes.wrong: She asked me what did I want.
mistakes.right: She asked me what I wanted.

why.en: Reported and indirect questions use statement order.
why.es: En la pregunta indirecta no hay did: what I wanted.

examples.en: Where do you usually have lunch?
Could you tell me where the lifts are?
I'd like to know how long the course lasts.
Do you know whether the museum opens on Mondays?
I wonder why she left so suddenly.
Which of these trains goes to Bristol?
Excuse me, do you have any idea what time the bank closes?
Who were you talking to when I came in?

explanation.en: After Could you tell me, use statement order: subject then verb.
Who is the subject, so there is no did: Who broke…?

practice.prompt: I'm not sure ___ the interview starts.

explanation.en: In an indirect question there is no do/does after the question word.

practice.prompt: Do you know ___ she is coming to the party?

explanation.en: A yes/no question becomes an indirect question with if or whether.
